newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand hits two-month high against dollar.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand hits two-month high against dollar.

text.p: The South African rand continued its New Year rally on Monday, reaching its strongest level in two months against the U.S. dollar.

The currency, which has enjoyed a wave of buying support from local and foreign investors this month, moved to below 4.60 on the dollar for the first time since November 29 in early trade. It was quoted at 4.5985/6035 at 0805 GMT.

Dealers said the rand was being buoyed by a market awash with dollars, as market operators bought the South African unit amid growing confidence that the fundamental economic picture should improve in 1997.

The rand fell nearly 30 percent against the dollar in 1996 on political and economic concerns, but economists say the outlook has brightened for this year with the current account on the balance of payments set to narrow sharply.
